Let me check the script logic against the code.

1. `load_households()` — loads all households (active_only=False default). Good.
2. `find_duplicates(households)` — returns groups of 2+ active household IDs. Good.
3. `kept_id = next(hid for hid in group if is_valid_household_id(hid))` — picks the valid one. If none valid, StopIteration — but ticket says keep the record whose ID is valid; presumably at least one is valid. Edge case but not necessarily wrong.
4. `set_status(other_id, "merged", merged_into=kept_id)` — set_status loads households, sets status and merged_into, saves. Only changes those two fields. Good. It ignores the "delete inactive households" note — correct per R2/ticket (no record deleted).
5. No new IDs. Good.
6. `save_households(load_households())` — reloads and saves. This writes the whole registry. But wait — set_status already saved each change. Then save_households(load_households()) re-reads and re-writes — this is a no-op rewrite of the same data. Fine, doesn't break anything.

One concern: set_status raises KeyError if household not found — IDs in group come from actual households, so fine.

Another concern: find_duplicates only considers active households. If a duplicate group includes an already-merged record, it's excluded — fine.

Potential issue: `next(hid for hid in group if is_valid_household_id(hid))` — if no valid ID in group, StopIteration crash. But ticket says duplicates have mistyped IDs, implying the other one is valid. Not a bug per ticket.

Also check: does set_status's merged_into field exist on Household? Yes, `merged_into: str | None = None`. Good.

Does the script modify only status and merged_into? set_status sets h.status and h.merged_into, saves. Yes.

The final save_households(load_households()) — writes the whole registry file with all households including inactive ones. load_households() without active_only returns all. Good — no deletion.

One subtle thing: the docstring says "Run once from the Lifeline root". sys.path insert of parent.parent — scripts/merge_duplicates.py, parent = scripts, parent.parent = repo root. Good.

Check store module? REGISTRY = "registry.json" — store.read_json presumably resolves to data/. Not critical.

Everything checks out. Accept.
